newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-BENJAMIN AND BISHOP SET UP VICTORY CHANCE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BENJAMIN AND BISHOP SET UP VICTORY CHANCE.

text.p: Pace pair Kenny Benjamin and Ian Bishop shared six Victoria wickets on Saturday to give West Indies the chance of a rare victory on their Australian tour.
West Indies, who trailed by 18 on first innings, fought back by dismissing Victoria for 197 in their second innings.
The touring side were 41 for one in pursuit of their winning target of 216 at the close of the third day of the four-day match.

Acting captain Brian Lara, controversially dismissed hit wicket for 86 in the first innings, was 14 not out and Sherwin Campbell was also on 14 after losing opening partner Adrian Griffith for one, leg before wicket to Paul Reiffel.
West Indies had resumed their first innings in the morning on 312 for five but suffered another worrying late order batting collapse ahead of next week's third test against Australia.
The last five wickets fell for just 11 runs for West Indies to be all out for 336. Middle-order batsman Jimmy Adams took his overnight score from 43 to 52 before falling to Reiffel.
Victoria all-rounder Ian Harvey instigated the collapse, taking three wickets in 11 balls without conceding a run to finish with five for 56 from 23.1 overs.
However, West Indies pace bowlers then made up for their team's deficiencies with the bat by tearing through the Victorian top order, reducing the home side to 52 for five shortly after lunch.
Opener Graeme Vimpani, who scored 133 in Victoria's first innings of 354, made 20 before he was caught behind by Courtney Browne off Benjamin.

Former Australia batsman and acting Victoria captain Dean Jones was top scorer with 33 but too few of his team mates were able to resist Benjamin, who took three for 53, and Bishop, who took three for 40.
